headline: Paper formalizes safety and retry costs for stateful agent execution harnesses
summary: The paper models an agent's tool-execution harness as a stateful Petri-net supervisor: approvals, capabilities and budgets become consumable marks, and an external kernel admits calls only when interface, validation, state and supervisor checks pass. Its proofs show safety for the specified model and give four assumptions needed to transfer that result to a running system. It also models the extra inference cost when an agent retries after refusal and derives a proposer-aware safe supervisor that can reduce that cost. The release-agent example is a synthesis illustration, not deployment evidence. Allowed-call argument attacks, bypasses and system correspondence need separate validation.
